name: Peter Hager
forbes_bio: Peter Hager is a major shareholder of Hager SE and also serves on the company's Supervisory Board.
The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.
Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.
Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.
The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC.

name: Chen Zemin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2014-2021); Hurun Global (2020-2023); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen is the cofounder and largest shareholder of Sanquan Food, one of China's largest frozen food producers.
Chen previously worked as a surgeon, a hospital vice president and a public health bureau official.
Chen's sons Chen Nan and Chen Xi are chairman and general manager, respectively, of Sanquan Food.
Chen's wife Jia Lingda is Sanquan's vice chairman.

name: David Helgason
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022); SEC insider holdings (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Iceland-born David Helgason cofounded game engine company Unity Software in 2004 in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Some of the world's most popular online and mobile games were built using Unity's engine, including Pokemon Go, Among Us and Overcooked.
In September 2020, Unity Software went public on the New York Stock Exchange; he owns a nearly 4% stake.
Helgason served as CEO from 2003 to 2014, and is still a board member, but spends most of his time as a venture capital investor.
Helgason and his cofounders started off creating a game that failed, but realized that their game engine had value for others.
forbes_facts: Helgason is one of just two billionaires from Iceland; the other is investor Thor Bjorgolfsson.
Helgason has a wide array of interests; he studied physics, Arabic, and psychology at the University of Copenhagen from 1997 to 2001.

name: Andrew MacMillan
forbes_bio: Andrew MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, America's largest private company.
His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
He's one of nine billionaire siblings who inherited stakes in the company from their father John H.  MacMillan III, who died in 2008.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

name: Antonio Luiz Seabra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2025)
forbes_bio: Antonio Luiz Seabra founded Natura Cosmeticos in 1969 as Brazil's answer to Avon and built it into Brazil's largest beauty company.
Some 1.4 million "consultants" (mainly women) sell Natura products door-to-door across Brazil, six other Latin American countries and France.
Natura Cosmeticos, which went public in 2004, bought U.K. cosmetics chain The Body Shop from L'Oréal in 2017 for over $1 billion.
Seabra is co-chairman of the board of Natura and also owns Bresco, a Brazilian property-rental operation focused on warehouses, offices and hotels.
Media-shy Seabra reportedly owns an apartment on the banks of the river Seine in Paris as well as real estate in London.
forbes_facts: Seabra communicates directly to employees through motivational videos. He is known for quoting poetry and philosophy in business meetings.

name: Daniel Yong Zhang
forbes_bio: Daniel Zhang has been the chairman of Chinese e-commerce heavyweight Alibaba Group since September 2019.
Zhang is also a member of the investment committee at Alibaba financial services arm Ant Group.
China held up Ant's planned dual listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong on regulatory concerns on November 3, 2020.
Zhang was the chief financial officer of online gaming firm Shanda Interactive Entertainment from 2005 to 2007.
Zhang resigned from the board at ride-sharing app DiDi Global in Dec. 2021; he left the board at social media firm Weibo in Jan. 2022

name: Mark Haoyong Yang
forbes_bio: Mark Yang, also known as Yang Haoyong, is the chairman of Guazi, an online site that sells second-hand cars.
Yang earlier founded online classified site Ganji, which was acquired by 58.com.
He holds degrees from Yale University and the University of Science and Technology of China.

name: Hary Tanoesoedibjo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2021)
forbes_bio: Hary Tanoesoedibjo got his start building a media business soon after college.
He stepped down as CEO of his Media Nusantara Citra (MNC), which owns four national TV stations, in 2016 to focus on politics.
In 2023, he opened the Lido Music & Arts Center in Bogor as part of the Lido City project, which will feature a Trump-branded golf course and resort.
His listed MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly MNC Land, in 2000. MNC Tourism is building another Trump-branded golf resort in Bali.
His daughter Angela, who used to serve as Indonesia's Deputy Tourism and Creative Economy Minister, became co-CEO of MNC Group in 2024.
forbes_facts: Hary, who attended Donald Trump's inauguration in 2017, is building a Trump Hotel luxury resort in Bali.
Hary is now actively involved in his political party Perindo, which he founded in 2014 after a brief run to be the country's vice president.

name: Patrick Zalupski
sec_insider_companies: Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (DFH) - President and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Patrick Zalupski is the founder, chairman and CEO of Dream Finders Homes, a Florida-based homebuilder.
Dream Finders Homes went public in January 2021 via an IPO.
Zalupski started the company in 2008 and focuses on first time homebuyers and move-up buyers--homeowners who are moving to a newer or bigger home.
The company builds homes in eight states, primarily in the Southeast.
forbes_facts: In 2009, Dream Finders' first full year of business, the company built just 27 homes. In 2022, it sold 6,878 homes.
